messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Canary rollout (canary-5732) is failing health checks and showing elevated 5xx rates (>6% over baseline). Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/d/rollouts/canary-5732

sara: saw the alert. quick check — are the failing checks the k8s liveness probes or our app-level health endpoint?

mike_r: looks like liveness probes are flapping. logs from the pod show lots of `connection refused` to internal redis before returning 503. snippet: `ERR connect ECONNREFUSED 10.2.5.11:6379`

arjun: hmm, we increased probe frequency for the canary to speed up detection (interval 5s). that likely made transient upstream drop look fatal. also saw a spike in CPU right before restarts.

sara: can we pause the canary / rollback traffic? I want to stop blast radius and decide next steps. tagging @arjun for perms.

mike_r: agree. recommend abort and revert traffic to stable. I'll watch metrics while it's rolled back.

sara: running abort now:```bash
# abort canary and immediately revert traffic
redwoodctl rollout abort --canary-id=canary-5732 --reason "liveness flapping -> 5xx spike"
```

devops-bot: Action: rollout abort requested by sara. Tracking ID: rbt-1840023456-01. Reverting traffic to stable...

devops-bot: Rollout abort complete. Traffic reverted to stable version v1.24.3. Canary pods scaled down.

mike_r: metrics after abort: 5xx rate in prod dropped from 5.9% -> 0.7% over 2min. latency returned to baseline. looks like abort worked.

emma: any customer-facing impact? we should check active sessions / API errors for paid customers and decide if we need an incident email.

mike_r: small batch of requests during the spike (~3:12-3:18 UTC) saw errors, volume low (~0.02% of total qps). no major customers reported. recommend monitoring and not emailing yet.

arjun: root cause hypothesis: increasing liveness probe frequency exposed transient redis connection failures caused by momentary network congestion on canary nodes -> kube restarted pods -> cascade of cold starts -> transient 5xx. two fixes: 1) revert probe interval back to 15s + add jitter, 2) harden redis client retry/backoff in canary variant.

sara: agree. actionable items: 1) disable canary routing (feature flag) 2) revert probe config in the canary deployment manifest 3) add client retries in next canary build.

sara: disabling FF now:```bash
ffctl toggle canary-routing false --env=prod --note "abort after liveness flapping"
```

devops-bot: Feature flag canary-routing set to false. Change takes effect immediately.

arjun: I'll prepare a revert PR for the k8s healthcheck change and include jitter/backoff notes. linking draft: https://git.redwood.ai/r/infra/healthchecks/pull/42

leo: heads-up: oncall handoff at +30m. if this isn't closed by then, please leave a short status and escalate to eng-sre.

emma: I'll monitor customer channels for 30m and ping sales if anything pops up.

mike_r: follow-up checks: I left a small dashboard panel comparing canary vs stable redis connection failure counts. will keep it up for 20m.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: mitigated. Event rbt-1840023456-01 closed by sara. Post-mitigation monitoring window: 15m. If error rate rises, reopen incident and page oncall.

arjun: for the postmortem, notes to include: avoid aggressive probe tuning during canaries, add network/redis throttling sim in canary tests, ensure client retries are enabled for experimental variants.

sara: confirmed stable. leaving handoff note for next oncall: the abort removed the canary, root cause likely probe tuning + transient redis connectivity on a subset of nodes. follow-up owners: arjun (infra change + PR), mike_r (metrics + dashboards), emma (customer comms).

leo: thanks all — I'll pick up at handoff. :thumbsup:

sara: thanks team. closing thread. :white_check_mark:
